links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of clinicians with vs without AI support; overreliance assessment
links.effect: Accuracy 57.14% with ADIS vs 66.67% without (nonsignificant); trainees 0% accuracy when ADIS wrong vs 68.75% when correct, indicating overreliance.
links.quote: Overall diagnostic accuracy was 57.14% when ADIS was active versus 66.67% without ADIS, a nonsignificant difference.

links.outcome: Whether clinicians detected incorrect AI suggestions; confidence when AI wrong
links.effect: Trainees showed 0% accuracy when ADIS was wrong vs 68.75% when correct; trained clinicians 66.67% and 56.25%; confidence high regardless of ADIS correctness.
links.quote: Despite these differences in accuracy, confidence was high regardless of ADIS correctness.

unlisted_practices: AI literacy training to mitigate automation bias (recommended, not tested)

screen.reason: The study evaluates clinician diagnostic accuracy and automation bias with and without an AI decision-support tool in a vignette-based study, but does not compare specific deployment practices or safeguards.
